rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Cover Story Logistics
card.instruction: Accept that a secret plan exists, then focus on schedules, witnesses, explanations, cleanup, and what everyone must remember.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Dad's surprise picnic, where can forty guests board the bus unseen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Outside my shop. Dad never goes there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell everyone to arrive separately so the neighbours don't mention a crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's offered to open the shop for me while I organise it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let him. Move boarding round the back, and everyone buys something before disappearing. What time does he count customers?

card.title: Cover Story Logistics
card.instruction: Accept that a secret plan exists, then focus on schedules, witnesses, explanations, cleanup, and what everyone must remember.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Mum's surprise party, we're saying you brought the cake on the nine o'clock bus?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. She'll ask why she didn't see my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The last bus leaves at eight. Can you claim you walked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She drove past me at half eight. I was empty-handed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the cake was already here. We need Dad to remember accepting it before his nap.

card.title: One Suspicious Detail
card.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and treat it as the clue that will expose the entire hidden story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That red thread on the empty frame will explain our missing painting. Who wore red?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Me. I wrapped the painting in my scarf. Please cancel the police.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The thread gives us the packing method. Where did your scarf go?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To your sister. You promised her the painting for her wedding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this thread connects my generosity to my police report. Fetch the wedding card; we'll reconstruct my promises.

card.title: One Suspicious Detail
card.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and treat it as the clue that will expose the entire hidden story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This coffee ring on our holiday map will explain where my keys went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're in your pocket. Can we leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the ring explains why we're late. What is it covering?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The kennels. You put your mug there when I asked who'd take the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's our entire delay: I hid the errand under breakfast. Trace that ring; we need to check every stop I drank over.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake vanished. Theft, accident, or the dog. I'm leaning theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog. Help me get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take his lead; check beneath the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole cake's underneath, upright. There's a note: 'Hide from dog.' Your handwriting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accident leads: mine, in remembering. Keep the dog outside while I check whether I've protected the champagne too.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.

card.title: Official Interpreter
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the final authority on what the impossible situation means, correcting every interpretation that threatens your version of reality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wardrobe isn't escaping. It's exercising its freedom of position.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's taking my work clothes down the road. Help me stop it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll escort it. Ask politely for your uniform; this is a free wardrobe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It wants rent for storing my shirts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a proposal, not a demand. Bring our tenancy agreement; a free wardrobe can negotiate its share of the bedroom.

card.title: Official Interpreter
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the final authority on what the impossible situation means, correcting every interpretation that threatens your version of reality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our doorway opens to yesterday. It's an extension, not a fault.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yesterday's me is coming through to complain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first visitor. Please make our extension welcoming.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says this is his house and we're the visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's confusing age with ownership. Show him today's mortgage payment; visiting hours end at six.

card.title: Prophecy Under Revision
card.instruction: Project absolute certainty about what happens next while quietly revising the prophecy whenever reality disagrees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the telescope ready. The moon will turn green at noon, exactly as I foretold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's noon. Still white.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Noon where the prophecy was written. We have six hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wrote it here. I lent you the pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An imported pen. The change will occur at its factory's noon. Keep watching while I check the label.

card.title: Prophecy Under Revision
card.instruction: Project absolute certainty about what happens next while quietly revising the prophecy whenever reality disagrees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Set our best plates out. A visitor wearing gold will bring us a fortune tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the plumber with brass fittings. I'll get his payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Working gold. Leave the money; he'll be bringing ours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His bill's enormous. We owe him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fortune, precisely. He'll bring us the opportunity to part with it. Keep the best plates out; he'll accept hospitality before payment.

card.title: Obviously One of Us
card.instruction: Act as though effortless acceptance of the bizarre premise proves you belong, and treat visible confusion as a personal risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've saved our invisible guest their usual chair. I remember everything from my trial dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the guest you're putting your coat on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The welcome draping, of course. I wanted my membership dinner to start properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're offering you their coat now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Mutual recognition. Help me find the sleeves; I'd hate to rush such an honour.

card.title: Obviously One of Us
card.instruction: Act as though effortless acceptance of the bizarre premise proves you belong, and treat visible confusion as a personal risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can introduce me to your cloud family. I know the salute: this hand means welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's rain. Shall I tell them you're new?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need. The previous clouds used it differently. Your family will appreciate the traditional greeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mother's raining directly on you. Come under my umbrella.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And refuse her welcome? Hold my phone; I'll greet your father with both hands.

card.title: Senior in the Strange
card.instruction: Treat yourself as an experienced guide to impossible customs, offering patient instruction while preserving one unexplained advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your first shadow banquet, bow until the host's shadow bows back. Take your time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You only nodded. Mine's still waiting, and dinner's starting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have a standing courtesy. Lower your head a little; let it see you mean it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now it's lying flat across the dining-room door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, a full welcome. Stay bowed while we step over; I'll bring your plate so you needn't offend it.

card.title: Senior in the Strange
card.instruction: Treat yourself as an experienced guide to impossible customs, offering patient instruction while preserving one unexplained advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To enter the mirror, introduce yourself backwards. Slowly; give your reflection time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You walked straight through. Could your reflection introduce me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We have a private arrangement. Try your surname first; I'll wait here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's asking yours how to get an arrangement. Neither will let me through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful conversation. Gently turn yours towards you; I'll distract mine. We'll practise introductions without discussing my terms.

card.title: The One Normal Thing
card.instruction: Remain modest while controlling the single ordinary resource everyone needs to survive the increasingly impossible situation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm just serving soup. This spoon's the last utensil that hasn't melted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're starving, and the soup's floating out of reach. Let me use it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll catch it for everyone. Send the smallest children first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's rising towards the ceiling. I'll lift you if you feed my daughter next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm only the server; you're the legs. Carry me from child to child, and I'll portion what we catch.

card.title: The One Normal Thing
card.instruction: Remain modest while controlling the single ordinary resource everyone needs to survive the increasingly impossible situation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This kitchen tile still has gravity. I'm just keeping a place for everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pull me down. I can't hold the ceiling much longer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my hand. One foot on my tile, please; leave room for your dad.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's floating out the window. Let me take your place and reach him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay as the anchor. Nothing grand; climb onto my shoulders and I'll allocate the next foothold.

transfer.action: I check {prop} against the real bus timetable.
transfer.opening: Fine, a secret operation. Who explains the extra car? {request}
transfer.response: Our story misses the last bus. {counter}
transfer.closing: I'm trying to get the intrigue home without an impossible fare.

transfer.action: I isolate the smallest mark on {prop}.
transfer.opening: Ignore the rest. Why exactly this mark? {request}
transfer.challenge: Can we discuss the whole story?
transfer.closing: After this small piece explains its very specific journey.

transfer.action: I move {prop} between two rival explanations on the table.
transfer.opening: Let's test the explanation, not just defend it. {request}
transfer.response: That answer changes which theory gets the next chance. {counter}
transfer.challenge: I thought you'd made up your mind.
transfer.closing: The evidence keeps insisting I leave it somewhere movable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the missing cake taken, dropped, or eaten by the dog? Describe the crumbs before choosing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. Were those crumbs present before dinner too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, after you fed it your slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft returns to contention. Start again with who opened the cupboard.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Competing explanations guide exact evidence questions; new details force A to shift theory rather than stack unconnected accusations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel was lost, stolen, or delivered elsewhere. Was it a bag or a box?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A box with handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivery error leads. Describe the lid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was tied, not hinged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'box' loses support. Let's establish the container before accusing a driver.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Competing explanations guide exact evidence questions; new details force A to shift theory rather than stack unconnected accusations.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The missing cake is theft, accident, or the dog. Keep all three on the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog moves into first place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on you too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft deserves renewed funding.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lights failed because of weather, wiring, or the caretaker's shortcut.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather withdraws gracefully.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker unplugged them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shortcut wins. Wiring can keep its dignity.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me again what happened between four and four-ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should match one of these two versions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stopped for coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where does coffee fit into the version with the bus?

transfer.action: I hold {prop} down as it starts to float.
transfer.opening: It's levitating, not escaping. Use the correct interpretation. {request}
transfer.response: My explanation is what makes this manageable. {counter}
transfer.closing: Not if we want to know which direction counts as contained.

transfer.action: I adjust the time on the prophecy beside {prop}.
transfer.response: The stars plainly meant the revised timetable. {counter}
transfer.closing: Only before the prediction's deeper meaning arrived.

transfer.action: I make room for {prop} beside an invisible guest and greet the guest.
transfer.opening: Of course I can see who belongs here. {request}
transfer.response: That was the salute for the previous cloud formation. {counter}
transfer.closing: Not to the eye of a newcomer. I've already greeted them.

transfer.action: I bow to the shadow of {prop} before touching it.
transfer.opening: Beginners address the object; veterans greet its shadow. {request}
transfer.response: The advanced shortcut comes after the first miracle. {counter}
transfer.closing: Then how would you know you had earned the shortcut?

transfer.action: I keep {prop} inside the one square of floor still accepting gravity.
transfer.opening: Nothing grand about me. Just the normal part that works. {request}
transfer.response: Bring it within reach of my ordinary spoon. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You're only standing on the floor.
transfer.closing: Exactly. Notice how unusual that useful service has become.
